key_observations: This was a light laptop-usage Saturday with substantial unobserved time.
The freelance opportunity from the previous day progressed materially: the prospect responded, a discovery call happened, and a revised proposal was sent.
The SaaS received a smaller but meaningful thread of work, moving from authentication research to implementation, testing, and evening verification.
The day did not contain a long uninterrupted workday, but the observed work blocks were tied to concrete outcomes.
The afternoon YouTube session appears to be leisure, while the later technical research was directly related to the SaaS evidence in the surrounding events.

priority_alignment.assessment: strong progress because a prospect advanced to a discovery call and revised proposal

important_uncertainty: Most of the day was offline and cannot be evaluated from desktop events.
The exact scope, budget, or likelihood of the prospective client's project cannot be inferred from the visible communication windows.
The authentication change was tested and reviewed, but successful tests do not establish that every production edge case is resolved.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Follow up on the revised proposal at an appropriate time while protecting a focused SaaS block to continue the authentication and MVP work.

things_not_to_do: Do not treat the large offline portions of Saturday as lost productivity.
Do not criticize the short leisure break simply because it occurred between work blocks.
Do not assume that a sent proposal means the freelance opportunity will convert to paid work.
Do not infer production correctness solely from the local test run and code review evidence.
Do not recommend filling the remaining weekend with additional screen time merely because laptop usage was low.
